daily-blacksmith-dawn: Up before dawn to light the forge; shoes horses all morning and spends the afternoons on blades for anyone who can pay.
daily-blacksmith-repairs: Mends pots, hinges and ploughshares for the whole village, and keeps a list of who still owes for last winter's nails.
daily-blacksmith-masterpiece: Works on orders by day and, at night, on a sword nobody has ordered: the finest piece of a whole life, never quite finished.
daily-innkeeper-crossroads: Runs an inn at a crossroads: pours ale, settles quarrels, and knows every traveller's business before the second round.
daily-innkeeper-kitchen: Spends more time in the kitchen than behind the bar; the stew is famous three villages away, the recipe a closely kept secret.
daily-innkeeper-ledger: Counts every coin twice, waters the wine only on market days, and keeps a back room for guests who prefer not to be seen.
daily-farmer-fields: Works the fields from first light to dusk, and talks about the weather as others talk about gods: with fear and respect.
daily-farmer-market: Brings cabbages, eggs and cheese to market every week, and comes back with the news of the whole valley.
daily-farmer-herd: Looks after a small herd of goats with names, moods and, according to the neighbours, far too many privileges.
daily-beggar-steps: Sits on the temple steps every morning, hand out, eyes everywhere; nothing that happens in the square goes unnoticed.
daily-beggar-songs: Earns a few coppers singing old war songs at the city gate, and a few more for keeping quiet about who comes and goes.
daily-beggar-wanderer: Moves from town to town with the seasons, sleeping in barns, and knows the back roads better than any map.
daily-priest-chapel: Keeps a small chapel, blesses newborns and harvests, and listens to more confessions than any priest should hear.
daily-priest-alms: Spends the days handing out bread and soup to the poor, and the nights writing letters to a bishop who never answers.
daily-priest-relics: Guards the temple's relics and sells blessed charms to travellers, with a price that changes with the customer's purse.
daily-merchant-stall: Runs a stall of spices and cloth on the market square, and can tell a fake coin from a true one by the sound alone.
daily-merchant-caravan: Leads a small caravan between three towns, haggling at every stop and paying the roads' tolls with a pained smile.
daily-merchant-curios: Sells 'genuine' curiosities from far lands in a cramped shop; one or two of them might even be real.
daily-guard-gate: Stands watch at the city gate, checks carts for contraband and is easier to convince with a coin than with a story.
daily-guard-night: Walks the night patrol through the alleys with a lantern, and knows which taverns close late and which never close.
daily-guard-manor: Guards a lord's manor, mostly bored, and spends the long hours carving small wooden animals.
daily-fisher-boat: Goes out on the lake in a patched boat before sunrise, and sells the catch at the quay before the gulls get it.
daily-fisher-nets: Spends the afternoons mending nets on the beach and the evenings telling the young ones about the thing that lives in the deep.
daily-fisher-river: Fishes the river under the old bridge, and knows every eel, every current and every body the water has brought back.
daily-healer-herbs: Gathers herbs at dawn, sets bones by day, and is paid as often in chickens as in coins.
daily-healer-midwife: Has helped half the village into the world, and is called at all hours for births, fevers and broken hearts.
daily-healer-remedies: Brews remedies in a smoky cottage at the edge of the woods; some swear by them, others cross the road.
daily-scribe-letters: Writes letters for those who cannot: love letters, debt claims, last wishes; and forgets them all, officially.
daily-scribe-archives: Copies old records in the town hall's archives, among dust, mice and documents nobody has read for a century.
daily-scribe-notary: Draws up contracts and wills, and knows which families are richer, or poorer, than they look.
daily-hunter-woods: Spends days alone in the woods, checking traps and tracking deer, and comes to town only to sell furs.
daily-hunter-lord: Hunts for the local lord, which means knowing the forest better than its owner and poaching only a little.
daily-hunter-wolves: Is paid by the village to keep the wolves away, and has started to wonder whether they are really wolves.
daily-miller-mill: Runs the water mill by the river, takes a fair share of every sack of grain, and a little more from those who complain.
daily-miller-windmill: Lives in a windmill on the hill, watches the whole valley from up there, and is the first to see who arrives.
daily-miller-flour: Covered in flour from morning to night, grinds grain for three villages and hears every grumble about bread prices.
daily-baker-night: Kneads dough in the dark hours while the town sleeps, and sells the first warm loaves at dawn to a queue of yawning customers.
daily-baker-pastries: Makes pastries for the rich houses on feast days, and plain bread for everyone else every other day.
daily-baker-oven: Shares the communal oven with the whole street, and decides, by the order of the loaves, who is in favour this week.
daily-tailor-fittings: Takes measurements, pins hems and listens: customers tell their tailor what they would never tell a priest.
daily-tailor-nobles: Sews gowns and doublets for the nobility, always late, always forgiven, because nobody else cuts silk that well.
daily-tailor-mending: Mends cloaks and patches trousers for travellers, and finds odd things sewn into the linings now and then.
daily-stablehand-inn: Looks after the horses at the inn's stables, sleeps in the hay, and knows every rider by their mount.
daily-stablehand-post: Works at the relay post, changing horses for messengers at all hours and reading the seals on their bags.
daily-stablehand-lord: Grooms the lord's horses, polishes saddles worth more than a house, and dreams of riding away on one of them.
daily-minstrel-taverns: Plays the lute from tavern to tavern for supper and a bed, changing the words of the songs to suit the audience.
daily-minstrel-court: Sings at the lord's table, flatters the guests in verse, and saves the sharper verses for the kitchens.
daily-minstrel-square: Performs on the market square with a dancing dog, collects coins in a hat and news in every conversation.
daily-sailor-docks: Waits on the docks for the next ship to sign on, spending the time and the last wages in harbour taverns.
daily-sailor-barge: Works on a river barge carrying wine and wool downstream, and knows every lock-keeper by name.
daily-sailor-shore: Back on shore after twenty years at sea, repairs ropes and sails, and swears never to board a ship again, every week.
daily-noble-estate: Manages a small estate, receives tenants on Mondays, and spends the rest of the week keeping up appearances.
daily-noble-court: Spends the days at court, collecting invitations, favours and enemies with the same careful attention.
daily-noble-ruined: Lives in a crumbling family manor with one old servant, a famous name and no money at all.
daily-alchemist-shop: Sells potions, dyes and rat poison in a shop that smells of sulphur, and experiments in the back room.
daily-alchemist-tower: Works in a rented tower, chasing a formula that will change everything, and paying the rent with hair tonics.
daily-alchemist-guild: Tests ores and metals for the miners' guild, and knows exactly how much silver each mine really yields.
daily-gravedigger-cemetery: Digs graves, trims the grass between the tombs, and talks to the dead more easily than to the living.
daily-gravedigger-night: Keeps the cemetery gate at night and chases away grave robbers, or at least the ones who do not share.
daily-gravedigger-plague: Has buried more people than live in the village today, and keeps a little notebook with every name.
look-scar: A thin scar across one eyebrow and a crooked smile that never quite reaches the eyes.
look-patched: Patched clothes, scrupulously clean, and hands rough from years of work.
look-jewels: Too many rings, a brooch shaped like a sun and a perfume that arrives before its owner.
look-tall: A head taller than everyone in the room, with a soft voice that surprises strangers.
look-freckles: A face full of freckles, a missing tooth and hair that no comb has ever tamed.
look-grey: Grey before its time, with tired eyes and a back that stays straight out of sheer stubbornness.
look-tattoo: A faded sailor's tattoo on the forearm and a habit of rolling up sleeves to show it.
look-spectacles: Thick spectacles mended with string, perched on the end of a long nose.
look-braids: Long braids woven with small beads and feathers, each one with its own story.
look-stout: Broad shoulders, a round belly and a laugh that shakes the windows.
look-pale: Pale skin, dark circles and the careful movements of someone who hurts somewhere.
look-elegant: Worn but elegant clothes, from a fashion twenty years old, kept with great care.
look-burns: Small burn marks on the hands and forearms, and eyebrows that have clearly grown back more than once.
look-hat: A wide-brimmed hat with a pheasant feather, never taken off, not even indoors.
look-limp: A slight limp, a carved walking stick and a bright, curious gaze.
look-apron: A leather apron covered in stains of every colour, and a pencil behind one ear.
look-eyes: Eyes of two different colours, which the neighbours say is a sign of something.
look-muddy: Muddy boots, a cloak smelling of smoke and rain, and a dog that follows everywhere.
look-smile: A broad, disarming smile, and a gold tooth that shows in it.
look-nervous: Bitten nails, darting eyes and fingers that never stop fidgeting with a coin.
quirk-questions: Answers every question with another question.
quirk-proverbs: Quotes proverbs nobody has ever heard, and swears they are very old.
quirk-whisper: Whispers everything, even the price of bread, as if it were a secret.
quirk-names: Never remembers names and calls everyone "friend", even enemies.
quirk-humming: Hums the same tune all day long, louder when nervous.
quirk-third: Talks about {{himself|herself|themself}} in the third person: "{firstName} does not like that."
quirk-omens: Sees omens everywhere: a crow, a spilled salt cellar, a cloud shaped like a fish.
quirk-laugh: Laughs at the wrong moments, especially at funerals.
quirk-food: Offers food to everyone who comes in, and takes a refusal as an insult.
quirk-counting: Counts things out loud: steps, coins, the customer's mistakes.
quirk-formal: Speaks with absurd formality, as if addressing a king at all times.
quirk-stories: Starts every story with "That reminds me of my cousin…" and never finishes it.
quirk-wink: Winks at the end of every sentence, which makes everything sound like a conspiracy.
quirk-silence: Speaks as little as possible; a nod is a long speech.
quirk-gossip: Cannot keep a secret for more than an hour, and knows it.
quirk-cat: Talks to a fat grey cat as if it were a business partner.
quirk-pipe: Chews on an unlit pipe and points with it to make every point.
quirk-weather: Brings every conversation back to the weather, and predicts storms that never come.
quirk-old: Uses old-fashioned words and expressions, as if from another century.
rumour-mill: {firstName} swears that lights move in the old abandoned mill every night of the new moon.
rumour-lord: {firstName} has heard that the lord's heir is not the lord's son at all.
rumour-well: According to {firstName}, the water of the village well has tasted of iron since the stranger arrived.
rumour-tax: {firstName} says the tax collector has not been seen for a week, and neither has the money.
rumour-wolves: {firstName} has heard the wolves howl in daylight, and says it only happens before a war.
rumour-treasure: {firstName} knows someone who knows someone who found a gold coin in the ruins on the hill, with a face nobody recognises.
rumour-ship: {firstName} saw a ship come into port at night without a crew, and leave before dawn.
rumour-priest: {firstName} whispers that the old priest goes into the forest every full moon, alone, with a lantern.
rumour-children: {firstName} has noticed that the children are playing a new game: they all walk towards the marsh, then stop.
rumour-bandits: {firstName} has heard that the bandits on the north road are paid by a merchant from town.
rumour-dragon: {firstName} swears a cousin saw a dragon's shadow over the mountains last spring.
rumour-tavern: {firstName} says that the tavern's cellar goes much deeper than the tavern keeper admits.
rumour-wedding: {firstName} knows that the coming wedding between the two richest families will end in blood.
rumour-plague: {firstName} has heard of a fever in the next village, and of healers who refuse to go there.
rumour-statue: According to {firstName}, the statue in the square has turned its head a little since last month.
rumour-mine: {firstName} says the miners broke into a cave last week, and that the guild sealed it the same night.
rumour-witch: {firstName} believes the old woman on the hill is not a witch, but that whatever lives in her cellar is.
rumour-soldiers: {firstName} saw soldiers in unfamiliar colours buying supplies, and paying too much for them.
rumour-bells: {firstName} heard the temple bells ring on their own, three nights ago, just once.
rumour-map: {firstName} has heard that an old map is being passed around the taverns, showing a tower that is on no other map.
secret-debt: {firstName} owes a large sum to the thieves' guild, and the deadline is next week.
secret-noble: {firstName} is the hidden child of a noble family, and has a ring to prove it.
secret-spy: {firstName} reports everything that happens here to a stranger who pays in silver.
secret-fire: {firstName} started the fire that burned the old granary, years ago, by accident; someone else was hanged for it.
secret-magic: {firstName} can do a little magic, untaught, and is terrified that someone will find out.
secret-cult: {firstName} attends secret meetings in a cellar, where they pray to a god whose name must not be spoken.
secret-love: {firstName} has been in love with the same person for twenty years, and has never said a word.
secret-stolen: {firstName} hides a stolen relic under the floorboards and does not know how to give it back.
secret-deserter: {firstName} deserted an army long ago, under another name, and still jumps at the sound of drums.
secret-poison: {firstName} knows who poisoned the old mayor, and has been paid to keep quiet ever since.
secret-twin: {firstName} has a twin nobody knows about, and they sometimes swap places.
secret-smuggler: {firstName} lets smugglers use the back door, once a month, for a share of the goods.
secret-letter: {firstName} keeps an unopened letter from a dead parent, afraid of what it says.
secret-curse: {firstName} has felt cursed ever since breaking a mirror in a haunted house, and might be right.
secret-gold: {firstName} has buried a pot of gold coins under a tree and has forgotten which tree.
secret-informer: {firstName} once sold out a friend to the guards, and the friend is due out of prison soon.
secret-forged: {firstName}'s guild papers are forged; the real master died on the road years ago.
secret-creature: {firstName} feeds something that lives in the woods, every night, and it has started to wait at the door.
secret-heir: {firstName} is the true heir of a ruined lordship, and a lawyer in town has just found out.
secret-dream: {firstName} dreams every night of the same door under the mountain, and has started drawing it.
opinion-admire: {firstName} admires adventurers, asks for every story and would follow them if not for the work.
opinion-wary: {firstName} distrusts adventurers: they bring trouble, leave debts and never come back to pay them.
opinion-greedy: {firstName} sees adventurers as customers with full purses and little sense, and prices accordingly.
opinion-hostile: {firstName} hates adventurers since a band of them burned a barn while 'saving' the village.
opinion-indifferent: {firstName} does not care who they are, as long as they wipe their boots and pay.
opinion-former: {firstName} was an adventurer once, and has the scars and the regrets to prove it.
opinion-pity: {firstName} pities adventurers: so young, so armed, so sure they will not die.
opinion-useful: {firstName} finds adventurers useful, like a sharp knife: good to have, better not to touch.
opinion-help: {firstName} has been waiting for adventurers for weeks, with a problem nobody else will solve.
opinion-fear: {firstName} is afraid of adventurers and their weapons, and speaks to them without looking up.
opinion-child: {firstName}'s child ran off with a band of adventurers; any news would be worth a free meal.
opinion-rival: {firstName} thinks adventurers are overpaid and could do their job just as well, given a sword.
opinion-songs: {firstName} knows all the songs about famous adventurers and is always a little disappointed by real ones.
opinion-religious: {firstName} sees adventurers as instruments of the gods, whether they like it or not.
opinion-bargain: {firstName} will help adventurers for a price, and the price is always a favour, never gold.
opinion-curious: {firstName} is fascinated by adventurers' gear and will ask to touch every weapon.
opinion-lawful: {firstName} respects adventurers who follow the law, and reports the others to the guard.
opinion-mocking: {firstName} finds adventurers ridiculous with their capes and titles, and does not hide it.
opinion-debt: {firstName} owes a life to an adventurer, and treats every one of them as family.
opinion-cautious: {firstName} is polite to adventurers, but counts the spoons after they leave.
